Title: Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property
Summary: One of the first international intellectual property treaties. It established national treatment and the right of priority, so an applicant who files a patent or trade mark in one member country has a period to file in others with the same priority date.

Title: Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
Summary: International agreement on copyright requiring members to protect works from other member countries without formalities such as registration, and setting minimum terms of protection for authors.

Title: Patent Cooperation Treaty
Summary: Lets inventors file a single international patent application that can later be pursued in many countries. It includes an international search and an optional preliminary examination before national phase entry.

Title: Madrid Protocol on the international registration of marks
Summary: Allows trade mark owners to seek protection in many countries through one application filed with their home office and administered by WIPO.

Title: Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS)
Summary: World Trade Organization agreement setting minimum standards for patents, copyright, trade marks, designs and other IP that member countries must provide, with dispute settlement for enforcement.

Title: WIPO Copyright Treaty
Summary: Updated international copyright rules for the digital environment, covering computer programs, databases and the legal protection of technological measures that restrict copying.

Title: Diamond v. Chakrabarty
Summary: United States Supreme Court decision holding that a genetically modified bacterium capable of breaking down crude oil was patentable subject matter, opening the way for biotechnology patents.

Title: Alice Corp. v. CLS Bank International
Summary: United States Supreme Court decision that claims to an abstract idea implemented on a generic computer are not patent eligible, reshaping the examination of software and business method patents.

Title: D'Arcy v Myriad Genetics
Summary: High Court of Australia decision that isolated genetic material coding for the BRCA1 gene was not a patentable invention, because the substance of the claim was genetic information rather than a manner of manufacture.

Title: Commissioner of Patents v Thaler (DABUS)
Summary: The Full Federal Court of Australia held that an inventor named on a patent application must be a natural person, overturning an earlier ruling that the AI system DABUS could be named as an inventor.

Title: Feist Publications v. Rural Telephone Service
Summary: United States Supreme Court decision that facts are not protected by copyright and that a telephone directory's white pages lacked the minimal creativity needed for protection.

Title: Authors Guild v. Google
Summary: The US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit found that Google's scanning of books to create a searchable index with short snippets was fair use.

Title: Creative Commons licences released
Summary: The first set of Creative Commons licences gave creators a simple, standardised way to grant the public permission to share and reuse their work on stated conditions.

Title: Attention Is All You Need
Summary: Research paper introducing the transformer, a neural network architecture based entirely on attention mechanisms that became the foundation of modern large language models.

Title: Efficient estimation of word representations in vector space (word2vec)
Summary: Introduced simple neural models that learn vector representations of words from large text corpora, where words with similar meanings end up close together.

Title: BERT: pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers
Summary: Research paper describing BERT, a language model pre-trained on unlabelled text that reads context in both directions and can be fine-tuned for many language tasks. Its architecture underlies many sentence embedding models.

Title: Visualizing data using t-SNE
Summary: Paper introducing t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding, a technique for visualising high-dimensional data in two or three dimensions that is particularly good at revealing clusters.

Title: UMAP: uniform manifold approximation and projection
Summary: Paper describing UMAP, a dimension reduction technique grounded in topology that is fast and tends to preserve more global structure than t-SNE.

Title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
Summary: Research paper reporting that the AlphaFold system predicts the three-dimensional structure of proteins with accuracy competitive with experimental methods.

Title: ChatGPT released to the public
Summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT, a conversational assistant built on a large language model, which reached a very large audience within weeks and prompted wide debate about generative AI.

Title: European Parliament approves the Artificial Intelligence Act
Summary: The European Parliament voted to adopt the AI Act, which regulates artificial intelligence systems according to their level of risk and sets transparency duties for general-purpose models.

Title: Paris Agreement
Summary: International climate agreement in which countries committed to limit global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, through nationally determined contributions reviewed over time.

Title: Kyoto Protocol
Summary: International treaty that committed industrialised countries to binding targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, with market mechanisms such as emissions trading.

Title: Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
Summary: Treaty phasing out chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting chemicals. It is widely regarded as one of the most successful environmental agreements.

Title: IPCC Sixth Assessment Report: synthesis report
Summary: Summarises the scientific assessment of climate change, its impacts and options for adaptation and mitigation, concluding that rapid and deep emissions cuts are needed this decade.

Title: Garnaut Climate Change Review final report
Summary: Independent review commissioned by Australian governments examining the impacts of climate change on the Australian economy and recommending an emissions trading scheme.

Title: On the antibacterial action of cultures of a Penicillium
Summary: Alexander Fleming's paper reporting that a mould contaminating a bacterial culture produced a substance that killed bacteria, later developed into penicillin.

Title: A programmable dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease (CRISPR-Cas9)
Summary: Showed that the Cas9 enzyme can be programmed with guide RNA to cut DNA at chosen sites, laying the groundwork for CRISPR genome editing.

Title: Unidentified curved bacilli in the stomach of patients with gastritis
Summary: Barry Marshall and Robin Warren reported bacteria in the stomachs of patients with gastritis and peptic ulcers, work later recognised with the Nobel Prize.

Title: Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine receives first authorisation
Summary: The United Kingdom's medicines regulator gave the first emergency authorisation of an mRNA vaccine against COVID-19.

Title: Human Genome Project declared complete
Summary: The international project announced it had sequenced essentially the whole human genome, providing a reference used across biology and medicine.

Title: James Webb Space Telescope launched
Summary: The largest space telescope yet launched, designed for infrared astronomy to observe the earliest galaxies, star formation and the atmospheres of exoplanets.

Title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
Summary: The first crewed Moon landing: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module and walked on the surface, with images relayed through stations including Parkes in Australia.

Title: Australian Space Agency begins operations
Summary: Australia established a national space agency to coordinate civil space activity and grow the domestic space industry.

Title: First image of a black hole
Summary: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration released the first image of a black hole's shadow, at the centre of the galaxy M87.
